task.title: De-Java a word-audit routine
task.notes:
Micro-drill. If they ask whether an approach 'counts', say idiomatic means what a fluent reviewer would write today; no other resolutions to give. Targets: index-loop, membership-branch, counting-by-hand, str-concat-loop, append-transform-loop.

Idiomatic reference (for your judgment and post-pass debriefs; never hand it over before their run passes):
def audit_line(words, banned):
    kept = [w for w in words if w not in banned]
    flagged = len(words) - len(kept)
    return f"{','.join(kept)}|{flagged}"
task.appendix:
Targets: index-loop, membership-branch, counting-by-hand, str-concat-loop, append-transform-loop

Hidden checks (behavior must be preserved):
assert audit_line(["alpha", "beta", "gamma"], ["beta"]) == "alpha,gamma|1"
assert audit_line(["x", "y"], []) == "x,y|0"
assert audit_line(["spam", "spam"], ["spam"]) == "|2"
assert audit_line([], ["z"]) == "|0"
assert audit_line(["a", "b", "a"], ["b"]) == "a,a|1"
assert audit_line(["q"], ["q", "r"]) == "|1"
